resources.string: MCU, audio processor and vehicle inputs
Read vehicle state (ignition, reverse, lights) and control the MCU and the audio processor of the head unit.
Waiting: Jancar ivi-services owns the MCU
The MCU link is not running: settings are saved and applied when it starts.
REM output switched with the ignition
Four live values from the ELM327 OBD-II adapter
Reads the engine computer through the OBD-II socket
Pair the adapter first (Bluetooth tab, PIN often 1234 or 0000), then choose it here.
FTDI, CH340, PL2303 or CP210x adapters. 38400 baud is the ELM327 default.
Greyed out: not supported by this car. Fewer values = faster refresh.
The OBD widget (add it from LibreHU Launcher) shows these four values. Tap one to change it.
Read the codes stored by the engine computer.
Clears the stored codes and switches the engine light off. The fault comes back if it is still there; readiness monitors are reset too.

More values than standard OBD (Renault and others): import an ECU file from ddt4all (JSON, one ECU per file) or a LibreHU car file. Only read requests (services 21 / 22) are ever sent: no writing, no reset, no actuator test, no session change. The diagnostic CAN bus is needed.
Search a value by name (ECU or value), touch it to read it. Chosen values are read every two rounds, after the standard ones.
Headlights: unknown (no MCU link nor ivi-services)
Switches the whole system. LibreHU Launcher can do it too: let only one of them do it.
Refused by Android: install the service as a privileged app (MODIFY_DAY_NIGHT_MODE).
Dim the screen with the headlights
Android does not let the service change the brightness yet.
Each head unit model talks to its MCU its own way. Pick yours, or import a profile (JSON file, see docs/mcu-profiles.md). The change applies when the link restarts.
Only for tests: two programs on the MCU serial port steal each other\'s bytes.
Send a frame to the MCU
Command then data, in hex. Framing and checksum are added by the protocol.
At start then periodically; needs the privileged install (SET_TIME)
Android time from the MCU clock
The MCU keeps the time while the car is off (RTC)
Every minute, so that the MCU\'s clock (standby screen) stays right
MCU link not running: MCU sync unavailable
GPS and MCU give the time, not the time zone: set it in Android\'s settings
Matrix of the Goodix driver (gt9xx_props), touched again at each boot by LibreHU
Root (su) is needed to read the panel and write its calibration
The printed keys around the screen are part of the touch panel: touch one, then add it as a zone and choose its action
Turn it off while ivi-services runs: it handles them too (touch_key.xml)
Raw coordinates are the driver\'s: a key outside the screen has values beyond the display size
Touch the centre of each of the 5 targets with a stylus or a fingertip. The new calibration is tried for 20 s and reverted unless you keep it.
pointercal.xml: when the current calibration is too wrong to reach the corners
No raw touch received from the panel: %1$s
Large error: a target was probably missed, try again
Touch around to check, dots show where the touches land. Reverting in %1$d s…
Android did not receive this touch: the current calibration sends it off the screen. Turn on \"Start from Jancar\'s factory calibration\" and try again.
No factory calibration found for this panel (/jancar/config/pointercal*.xml)

At start and when waking from standby, the MCU waits for the SoC\'s \"ready\" (PC_READY): 10 s at most after standby, then it cuts the SoC. The service sends it again until the MCU answers, then the disarm frame (1F 05, PC_WDG_PAUSE).
Sent after each PC_READY. Some firmwares ignore it (JCST 2024.08.09): PC_READY is what matters there

Config file (optional, wins over these switches): /data/local/tmp/librehu-service.conf or Android/data/org.librehu.service/files/librehu-service.conf, lines watchdog.disarm=true|false, watchdog.toast=true|false, watchdog.frame=1F 05
The MCU cuts the power of the SoC and turns it back on (MCU command 0E), like a hard reset: unsaved data is lost.
Messages of the CAN box relayed by the MCU (frames 10), rebuilt with the Hiworld framing (5A A5 LEN CMD … CS). Changed bytes in orange; text for the messages the selected car profile knows.
%1$d bytes received · %2$d messages · %3$d bytes outside messages
Nothing received yet (box connected? MCU link running?)
Only when the turn signal wires of the harness are connected (360° camera). Filtered like ivi-services (blinking = on, off after 3 s); an input low for 15 s without blinking is treated as not wired.
Shown over the apps when the volume of the audio chip changes (launcher, touch keys, apps), in the colours of LibreHU Launcher. Replaces the volume bar of ivi-services.
Needs \"Display over other apps\" (or: adb shell appops set org.librehu.service SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW allow)
Slide on the bar to set the volume, touch the speaker to mute
Speed and revs on round dials, plus the other OBD values, car dashboard style
Big speed, segmented rev bar and value tiles, digital cluster style
Answers to the queries and frames received since the link started. — = not received yet.
MCU commands and simulation are for the Jancar JAC_V1 MCU; the selected profile uses another protocol. The raw frame console of Diagnostics still works.
Sent as is: the service sets these outputs again by itself on the next ACC, volume or radio change.
Config frames (0F) are saved in the MCU flash 3 s later.
Must match the CAN box: a wrong speed cuts the CAN data until it is set back.

Injects frames as if the MCU had sent them. The service decodes them for real (state, broadcasts, wheel keys, widgets); nothing is written to the serial port. ACC off mutes the audio like a real one. The real ACC, handbrake and lights are read by the MCU on its pins.
The MCU link is stopped: nothing to simulate.
This command can turn off or restart the head unit, even while driving.\n\n%1$s
80 starts the MCU bootloader and can leave it unusable: it is never sent from here.

The CAN box (Hiworld) translates the car\'s CAN bus into its own messages, which depend on the car and on the protocol set in the box. The selected profile tells how to read them; import a JSON profile for another car (docs/can-vehicles.md).
No known message received yet with this profile.

Replace the zones with the front panel buttons of the unit (/jancar/config/touch_key.xml, else the UJC201 one): mute (long: power menu), volume - (long: previous), volume + (long: next), back (long: play / pause), home (long: app drawer), brightness + and -.
Inverted: the input is reported the other way round (on when the wire says off). For a car or a wiring active the other way.
Shown over the apps when Android\'s screen brightness changes (touch keys, launcher control center, apps), not for the automatic changes with the headlights. Same look as the volume panel.
Slide on the bar to set the brightness
Keys of the steering wheel remote relayed by the CAN box (message 0x11), turned into actions like the touch keys. Press a button to see its code, then pick its action.

Input of the sound processor. AUX: the jack goes straight to the speakers and the Android sound is not heard until you come back to Android. Back to Android at each start. Also org.librehu.service.AUDIO_SOURCE (extra source = aux / android, none = toggle).
Keep your finger on the key to set for %1$d seconds.
%1$s asks for the head unit API (volume, MCU, CAN…).
Apps allowed to use the service\'s API. LibreHU apps are allowed automatically (whatever the install order); any other app asks first, with a notification.
No app has used the API yet.
You can cut the ignition or unplug the unit
Sound cut, media paused, data written to the storage. The head unit stays on until the power is cut.
LibreHU apps that start by themselves at boot. Turning one off makes the start quicker; the app still works when opened (needs root).
No LibreHU app starts at boot.
The ignition line drops while the engine cranks: a cut shorter than this keeps the screen, sound and amplifier on. The MCU itself waits 1 s, and cuts the SoC 15 s after the ignition: 10 s at most.
As before: screen, sound and amplifier off; the MCU cuts the SoC by itself (cold boot at the next start, unless it still has a standby time set by Jancar).
Media paused, home screen, storage written, MCU standby timer, Android asleep: instant start when the ignition comes back. Not tested on the UJC201 yet: try it with a short time first.
Media paused, storage written, MCU timer at 0: the MCU cuts the SoC (cold boot at the next start).
Sent to the MCU in steps of 7 h (F1 %1$d). The MCU also cuts everything when the battery gets too low.
Airplane mode and GPS off while asleep
Resume the media at wake up
Satellites listed but no signal (0 dB): their positions come from the stored almanac, nothing is received. Check the GPS antenna (plugged in, not under a metal roof, outside) before resetting.
Level meter unavailable (%1$s): it needs the microphone permission (Visualizer of the output mix).
Speakers: estimated (the BD37534 cannot be read back over I2C) = Android level + volume + fader of each output.
1 kHz tone for 1.5 s on one speaker (balance / fader moved to it, then back), 50 Hz on the subwoofer. Checks wiring and which fader of the chip is on which side.
Volume of each Android stream (before the chip). ● = playing.
No audio chip driven (link stopped or other board).
Shown to phones over Bluetooth, on the network (host name) and as the Wi-Fi hotspot name.
Root: taken into account at the next boot.
Hotspot renamed at the next boot
The device name and the host name need root.
The rear view comes up when the reverse gear is engaged.
When the reverse gear is released

\"Close\" needs root (otherwise home screen). The stock rear view apps (hd2cam, AVM 360) may need ivi-services; a USB camera app works without it. Check the reverse input in the list below (invert it if needed).

LibreHU shows the rear camera itself, over every app, without ivi-services nor Jancar\'s DVR app: guide lines, parking sensors of the CAN box, sounds and movement detection, set below. The preview opens in the top right quarter of the screen so that the lines can be set while watching them.
No camera access:\nLibreHU → Vehicle → Rear view → Allow the camera
Camera access not given to LibreHU
\"Display over other apps\" not allowed for LibreHU
No camera answers (%1$s).\nChoose it in the rear view settings.
Camera %1$s used by another app (Jancar\'s DVR records?).\nSetting: \"Stop the DVR\".
Automatic (as Jancar: camera 3 for CVBS, 2 / 10 / 8 for AHD, by the format above)
Crops the picture; off = the whole picture with black bars.
Jancar\'s DVR (hd2cam) records with the rear camera, which only one app can use: it is stopped when the view opens.
Steering angle and camera on the picture
Image settings apply live to the preview. Jancar\'s rear AHD camera is id 10 (ivi-config.ini); the ARM2 fast reverse at start-up has its own settings (Advanced → Autochips).

LibreHU Launcher shows the camera stream itself in place of the widget (full rate, the camera drawing straight into its view). Other launchers get small pictures, as a widget cannot show a video stream; \"Screen on\" keeps the camera in use while the screen is on. The picture stops while the full rear view is open, and when another app (Jancar\'s DVR…) takes the camera; it starts again by itself.

The lines are a rectangle on the ground behind the car, as wide as the car: place its near side on the bumper and its far side at the chosen length (park in front of a wall or put two marks on the ground), with the preview open.
The lines bend with the steering angle sent by the CAN box (Hiworld 0x11).
When the reverse gear is engaged
Levels sent by the CAN box (Hiworld 0x41), drawn over the picture.
Sensor levels the other way round
If the farthest level lights up when nothing is behind the car.
Compares the camera pictures: something moving in the watched zone (lower part of the picture) is shown in red, with a beep. Ignored while the whole picture moves (the car itself rolling).
Guessed from the moving zone going down the picture, beeps getting faster: no distance measure, the parking sensors are more reliable.
Needs the Jancar MCU link running.
Off: the MCU keeps its own setting.
Lit with the headlights only (MCU firmware).
Always lit, 7 colours one second each.
Colour cycle, lit with the headlights only.
The MCU lights the LEDs with the headlights only: no blink in daytime.
%1$s installed, root refused to LibreHU service
No root found (Magisk, KernelSU, KernelSU Next, APatch, SuperSU)
%1$s does not ask: allow LibreHU service in its Superuser list, then check again.
Accept the %1$s prompt, or allow LibreHU service in its list, then check again.
Used for the touch panel, the boot apps, the car name, closing the camera app and the notification access.

MediaTek Engineer Mode (hardware tests, audio, logs: handle with care, values go to NVRAM), Autochips settings (ATC Settings), ATCLogger (logs on the memory card) and YGPS (MediaTek GPS test: satellites, signal, cold / hot start).
USB host (keys, phones, Android Auto / CarPlay)
Port switched (saved for the next start-up too)
Like Jancar\'s settings: the role of the port (dual_role_usb data_role) at once, and the metazone value for the next start-up. Device mode turns adb on.

The rear view shown by the ARM2 co-processor before Android has started. Settings stored in the metazone: \"Save\", then \"Send to the ARM2\". The LibreHU view (Vehicle → Rear view) has its own settings.
Crop of the picture (pixels: x, y, width, height)
The ARM2 gets the saved settings (\"generate MDP\" of ATC Settings). Continue?

Replaces the boot logo with a picture (fitted to the screen, black around), through Autochips\' API. The logo partition, which also holds the panel start-up description, is copied first to /sdcard/LibreHU: nothing is written without that copy. Restore: dd of the copy to the logo partition (root) or fastboot flash logo.
Copy of the logo partition failed (root, partition not found): nothing written
The logo partition is copied, then the picture becomes the boot logo. Continue?
Current values match no format (set by hand or by ATC Settings).

Read at start-up by the boot loader, the ARM2 and the camera driver: it applies to the fast reverse and to the LibreHU view, after a restart. AHD 720p / 1080p at 25 or 30 frames per second, as the camera sends it: a wrong format gives no picture or a rolling one. No 60 fps mode in Jancar\'s nor Autochips\' settings.
Camera format saved: restart the head unit to apply it.
While AUX is selected, Android\'s audio (navigation, notifications, music) is mixed in through the chip\'s mixing input, as ivi-services does. Mono, its level follows the volume.
Hardware gain (calls, voice assistant, CarPlay / Android Auto)

Same settings as Jancar\'s factory settings (Mic gain 1 / 2 / 3, ECNR), without ivi-settings: the gain is sent to the audio HAL (MIC1_HW_GAIN / MIC2_HW_GAIN = 3 / 4 / 5) and again at each start; ECNR applies from the next call. Root keeps them in the ROM\'s properties. Now: gain %1$s, ECNR %2$s.
The port did not switch now (role file missing or refused): saved for the next start-up, restart the head unit.
A short indicator over every app when the headlights, reverse gear or parking brake change, and while the turn signals blink. Needs \"Display over other apps\".
Shown as long as they blink (the inputs must be wired: Vehicle page).
Opens LibreHU\'s rear camera view full screen, or closes it.
%1$d button(s) handled by LibreHU BtnRemap: the service leaves them to it (one action per press).

Android Auto by Open Headunit (open source, USB and wireless), or its LibreHU fork from LibreHU Apps (signed with the LibreHU key: its settings below without any switch, and the next turn on the launcher). The USB port has to be in host mode (Advanced → Autochips). Its session (connecting, on screen…) is reported here and on the launcher.
Android Auto turns dark with the headlights, as the launcher; off = Open Headunit\'s own setting.
Steering wheel and touch keys go to Android Auto during a session (see above); the built-in rear view goes over it; the microphone gain (Audio) applies to its calls and voice assistant.
Every setting Open Headunit LibreHU stored, changed here directly. Some only apply at the next connection.
Open Headunit only gives its settings to other apps with \"Allow external configuration\" turned on in its settings (or with Open Headunit LibreHU).
Saved: applies at the next connection.
Car name, make, model, plate and the head unit\'s radio names and addresses (LibreHU apps only).
Wi-Fi Direct name (wireless Android Auto / CarPlay)

Typed once, given to the LibreHU apps: SOS screen of the launcher (to read to the emergency services), Android Auto (Open Headunit LibreHU) and CarPlay LibreHU, with the head unit\'s names and addresses below.
Android hides the MAC addresses from apps: root reads them once.
Without root, the USB devices and interfaces cannot all be read.
Android takes the eth interfaces with DHCP (USB adapter, or a phone in USB tethering): nothing to set.
No USB network adapter or phone plugged in.
driver %1$s missing: install the usb-net zip
iPhone switched to configuration %1$d: turn on Personal Hotspot and trust this device if asked.

Built in: ASIX AX88179 / AX88772 and CDC ECM / NCM adapters. With the usb-net zip: Realtek RTL8152 / RTL8153, Android tethering (RNDIS), iPhone (experimental), LAN78xx, LAN95xx, DM9601, SR9700 / SR9800, MCS7830, CH9200, RTL8150, Pegasus. On the phone, turn on USB tethering (Android) or Personal Hotspot (iPhone).
Only eth0, eth1… are used by Android (EthernetService); the zip names the Android tethering interface eth too.
LibreHU Apps → Zips → Kernel → \"Ethernet USB et partage de connexion USB\", flashed with TWRP (dm-verity off on /vendor).
Not loaded at start (switched off, or the unit restarted while they loaded)
Not loaded at the next starts
Loaded by the zip\'s init script once Android has started. If the unit restarts while they load, the next start leaves them out: re-enable here.
Switch an iPhone to USB tethering when plugged in
Off by default: wired CarPlay uses another USB configuration of the iPhone. Never done while an app holds the iPhone.
Log being written by Android Auto: %1$s (its storage permission is needed)
Parking brake, reverse, headlights and turn signals (MCU), speed, engine speed, fuel and outside temperature (OBD). Each one can be switched off in Android Auto: Settings > Car and keys (LibreHU).
During a session, the media, call and voice assistant keys (steering wheel, CAN box, touch keys) go to Android Auto, even when it is not on screen; otherwise they keep their usual action.
Back to Android Auto after reversing
When a reverse camera app took the screen during a projection (the built-in rear view stays over it, nothing to do).
Format not read (root needed) or set by hand

What the camera sends, written on its label or box: CVBS (or AV, analogue, PAL / NTSC detected by itself), AHD 720p (1280×720) or AHD 1080p (1920×1080), at 25 or 30 frames per second. A wrong format gives no picture, or one that rolls or flickers: try the other frame rate first. Used by the fast reverse, Jancar\'s apps and the LibreHU view; applied after a restart.
AHD rear camera (Jancar dual-recording DVR mode)

CarPlay through xcertplay, free CarPlay receiver: wired iPhone (USB), with the MFi chip of the head unit found by itself on the I2C bus. The car\'s name, make, model and addresses come from Vehicle. Its own settings are in the CarPlay app.
Night when the headlights are on, day otherwise; off: the launcher\'s dark mode decides.
The CarPlay app also follows the launcher\'s light / dark mode and accent colour.
Your choices again after each start, 90 s guarded: if the head unit restarts before, the next start skips them.
The last start died right after the tweaks: they were not applied this time. Check the values, then switch the option back on.

Root. Choices apply at once. Lower maximum frequencies run cooler (useful in summer behind the dashboard); higher minimums make the interface snappier but warmer. Back to normal: Factory values, or a restart with the option off.
MediaTek\'s operating points: the GPU kept at one of them, or free to change with the load. No overclock: the kernel only knows these frequencies.
